note: getProcessor reads only the test field useTypes (recorded as a boolean in every record: false after setUp, true in the six methods that set it: testRewriteEqualitySame_useColors, testNotRewriteEqualitySame_useColors, testRewriteFunction, testRewriteTopObject_skippedToAvoidRewritingGBigint, testRewriteGBigInt_skipped and testRewriteInterface_optimized) and getName(); the varargs parameter is passed as an AbstractPeepholeOptimization[] array. setUp's enableTypeCheck/replaceTypesWithColors/disableCompareJsDoc (and the per-test repeats of the last two) and the constructor's super(MINIMAL_EXTERNS + EXTERN) (defaultExternsInputs) are restored from harness.fields. The createCompiler override returns a plain Compiler (harness.effective.createCompiler) after J2clSourceFileChecker.markToRunJ2clPasses(compiler), which only sets the compiler's runJ2clPasses flag; without it J2clEqualitySameRewriterPass.beginTraversal records shouldRunJ2clPasses=false and optimizeSubtree never rewrites. The DSL has no createCompiler hook, so (as in J2clClinitPrunerPassTest, batch 27) the descriptor makes the same call on the same compiler from getProcessor: the list evaluates its items in order (the void markToRunJ2clPasses call yields null, then the pass) and get(1) returns the pass. Equivalent because the flag's only readers in src/ are the J2CL passes and ProcessDefines; between createCompiler and getProcessor the harness only parses, type-checks and converts types to colors, none of which reads the flag; the call is idempotent (getNumRepetitions is 1). The expected-output parse uses a separate createCompiler() compiler that runs no J2CL pass, so its missing flag is unobservable.
